raw_case_text:
A 16-year-old female patient was admitted during the summer with a 4-day history of diffuse myalgia, retro-orbital headache, abdominal pain, fever, and chills. On admission, the patient looked pale and icteric, with tachycardia (123/min), palpable liver 1 cm below the right costal border, and the spleen was not palpable. The patient's blood pressure was normal. Arterial oxygen saturation in room air was 99%. The patient had Sbeta+-thalassemia (genotype S/thal beta), and the average laboratory data from outpatient follow-up was serum hemoglobin concentration (Hb) 11.7 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 62 fL, leucocyte count of 6.7 x 109/L, and platelet count of 123 x 109/L. The patient did not use hydroxyurea.
The initial laboratory test results are presented in Table 1. Metabolic acidosis was detected (pH 7.29; pCO2 28 mmHg; HCO3 13.8 mmol/L). Serology for viral hepatitis (A, B, and C) was non-reactive. Abdominal ultrasound revealed hepatosplenomegaly, moderate ascites, and bilateral pleural effusion without detection of gallstones or dilatation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts. Based on the local epidemiological, clinical, and laboratory data for a SCD patient along with serological confirmation of dengue (IgM reagent - risk group D according to the criteria of the Brazilian Ministry of Health), the diagnosis of SCIC associated with dengue (dengue hemorrhagic fever) was considered. The patient was treated with vigorous hydration, analgesia, transfusion of packed red blood cells to achieve a target hemoglobin S (HbS) concentration < 30% (exchange transfusion), and intravenous antibiotic therapy (ceftriaxone 2 g/day).
Twelve hours after admission, the clinical condition worsened with the onset of respiratory distress, drowsiness, and intensification of abdominal pain with rapidly increasing hepatosplenomegaly (spleen and liver palpable at the level of the iliac crests). Laboratory parameters deteriorated with intensifying anemia, elevated LDH, and kidney and liver dysfunction (Table 1). Further management included maintenance of packed red blood cell transfusion (achieved HbS 19.8%) and supportive measures such as hemodialysis and mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit. There was worsening organ failure, and the patient died eight days later.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 16-year-old female presenting with diffuse myalgia, retro-orbital headache, abdominal pain, fever, and chills for four days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 16-year-old female with Sbeta+-thalassemia presented with a 4-day history of diffuse myalgia, retro-orbital headache, abdominal pain, fever, and chills. On admission, she was tachycardic, pale, and icteric with hepatomegaly. Twelve hours following admission, she developed acute clinical deterioration with severe respiratory distress, drowsiness, worsening abdominal pain, and massive rapid hepatosplenomegaly extending to the iliac crests, progressing to multi-organ failure.
subjective.past_medical_history: Sickle cell-beta+-thalassemia (genotype S/thal beta); baseline labs: hemoglobin 11.7 g/dL, MCV 62 fL, WBC 6.7 x 10^9/L, platelets 123 x 10^9/L; not on hydroxyurea.
subjective.review_of_systems: Abdominal pain, chills, retro-orbital headache; no history of baseline vaso-occlusive crises on hydroxyurea.

objective.physical_examination: Admission: Pale, icteric, heart rate 123 bpm (tachycardia), blood pressure normal, SpO2 99% on room air; liver palpable 1 cm below the right costal margin, spleen not palpable. Deterioration (at 12 hours): Drowsy, acute respiratory distress, severe abdominal distention with massive hepatosplenomegaly (liver and spleen palpable to the level of the iliac crests).
objective.routine_investigations: Admission: Metabolic acidosis (pH 7.29, pCO2 28 mmHg, HCO3 13.8 mmol/L). Serial labs: Progressive severe anemia, markedly elevated LDH, acute renal failure, and severe hepatic dysfunction. Viral serologies: Hepatitis A, B, and C non-reactive. Abdominal ultrasound: Hepatosplenomegaly, moderate ascites, and bilateral pleural effusion, without gallstones or biliary ductal dilatation.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Confirmed Dengue virus infection (dengue hemorrhagic fever with plasma leakage, polyserositis, and severe thrombocytopenia) triggering fatal sickle cell intrahepatic cholestasis (SCIC) and acute splenic sequestration in a patient with sickle-beta+-thalassemia. Confirmatory testing showed Dengue IgM reagent (Risk Group D). Viral hepatitis A, B, and C and biliary obstruction were ruled out.
Plan & Outcome: Treated with vigorous intravenous hydration, analgesia, empiric IV ceftriaxone (2 g/day), and exchange blood transfusions targeting HbS < 30% (achieved HbS 19.8%). Following rapid decompensation with refractory lactic acidosis, multi-organ failure, and massive hepatosplenomegaly, she was transferred to the ICU, intubated for mechanical ventilation, and placed on continuous renal replacement therapy / hemodialysis. Despite maximal intensive supportive therapy, multi-organ dysfunction worsened, and she succumbed eight days after admission.
